messages.content: Help me signal the end of an XML element with the qualified name `{namespaceURI='http://www.example.com', localPart='item', prefix='ex'}` and augmentation information `augmentations` in an XML processing application that uses namespaces?

function.name: XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement
function.description: Signals the end of an XML element, handling namespace-related processing if namespaces are enabled, or delegating to the document handler otherwise. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

element.description: The qualified name of the element that is ending. Use QName object, has a constructor that takes in three parameters, namespaceURI, localPart, prefix This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

augs.description: Augmentation information associated with the element. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the tool "XMLNamespaceBinder_endElement" from namespace functions. Provide arguments as JSON.

The element argument should be a QName constructed with namespaceURI, localPart, prefix. But we can't actually construct objects; just provide string representation maybe like `"QName('http://www.example.com','item','ex')"` but spec says it can be any type of Java object in string representation. So likely pass something like `"new javax.xml.namespace.QName(\"http://www.example.com\", \"item\", \"ex\")"`? Or simpler: use string representation of QName: e.g., `"{'namespaceURI':'http://www.example.com','localPart':'item','prefix':'ex'}"`

But guidelines say: "Use QName object, has a constructor that takes in three parameters". We might represent as `"javax.xml.namespace.QName(namespaceURI=\"http://www.example.com\", localPart=\"item\", prefix=\"ex\")"`.

Let's produce:

{
    "element": "\"{namespaceURI=\\\"http://www.example.com\\\", localPart=\\\"item\\\", prefix=\\\"ex\\\"}\"",
    "augs": "\"augmentations\""
}

Wait quoting inside quotes may cause confusion. Maybe better to send raw strings without outer quotes because they will be parsed into JSON values. For example:

{
   "element":"{namespaceURI=http://www.example.com, localPart=item, prefix=ex}",
   "augs":"augmentations"
}

Yes that's fine. Let's do that.
